cards.evidence_claim: C&C Pizza Restaurant posts Friday and Saturday hours from 10 a.m. to midnight.

cards.evidence_claim: Pizza City’s ordering page lists hours until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Douglass Pizza & Grill
cards.subtitle: 298 George St, New Brunswick
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s official site before walking over, especially on Friday or Saturday when it posts its latest closing time for pizza and grill items.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten public, under-21-safe Rutgers–New Brunswick places where the stated activity needs no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Walk Helyar Woods
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Take the marked woodland trails with a friend; pause at the meadow, springs, and research pine forest, then leave before the Gardens gate closes.
cards.short_summary: A nearly 60-acre old-growth woods walk within Rutgers Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens lists Helyar Woods as a nearly 60-acre forest with hiking trails, and states that its grounds have no admission fee.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday; seasonal hours are 8 a.m.–7 p.m. Apr. 1–Sep. 30 and 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Oct. 1–Mar. 31. Trails can be uneven.

cards.entity_name: Edwin J. and Ida M. Otken Memorial Garden
cards.title: Meet by the Giant Chairs
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Use the oversized Adirondack chairs as an easy meetup point, then follow the stone paths through the mixed border of shrubs and grasses.
cards.short_summary: A photogenic garden centered on oversized Adirondack chairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens identifies the Otken Memorial Garden and its oversized Adirondack chairs; the Gardens states there is no admission fee.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; stay on paths and do not enter garden beds.

cards.title: Take a Quiet Rain Garden Loop
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Enter from the Rhododendron or Sun and Shade Garden trail and use the benches for a calm catch-up beside the pond and native plantings.
cards.short_summary: A shaded garden loop with benches, stone paths, and a small pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens describes the Rain Garden’s benches, pond, stone paths, and stormwater-focused plantings; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; uneven stone paths may be slippery after rain.

cards.title: Spread Out on the Evergreen Lawn
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Bring a blanket for a conversation or reading break on the lawn, then look closely at the pines, spruces, firs, and cedars around it.
cards.short_summary: An evergreen garden with an open lawn suited to a low-key break.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens describes the DeBoer Evergreen Garden lawn as a site for study breaks and blanket picnics; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; use a blanket rather than expecting picnic tables.

cards.title: Do a Holly Spotting Stroll
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Walk the collection slowly and compare American holly, winterberry, and hybrid specimens; keep wildlife viewing at a respectful distance.
cards.short_summary: A large collection of mature holly trees, including American hollies.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens describes the Holly Collection as one of the country’s largest American holly collections; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; do not pick berries or other plant material.

cards.title: Find a Bench Under the Canopy
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Follow the winding mulch paths together and pick a bench for a phone-free catch-up among rhododendrons, dogwoods, and spicebush.
cards.short_summary: A sheltered garden of rhododendrons and mature trees with benches.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens describes the Rhododendron Garden’s winding paths, tree canopy, and benches; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; paths are mulched and may be uneven.

cards.title: Watch the Pollinator Garden
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Stand quietly at the garden edge and see what birds, bees, bats, or butterflies appear among the habitat plantings beside Helyar Woods.
cards.short_summary: A habitat-focused garden bordering Helyar Woods.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens says the Pollinator Garden supports birds, bees, bats, and butterflies through curated habitat plantings; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; observe wildlife without handling it or disturbing habitat.

cards.title: Cool Off Beneath the Shade Trees
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Walk beneath the mature lindens, oaks, buckeyes, and magnolias; use this broad, shaded section for a slower conversation on a warm day.
cards.short_summary: A mature tree collection with extensive shade and spring blooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens describes the Shade Tree Collection’s mature trees and extensive shaded areas; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; remain on designated paths and respect planted areas.

cards.title: Circle the Seasonal Display Garden
cards.subtitle: Rutgers Gardens, Cook Campus
cards.notes: Take a short lap around the seasonal beds and compare the bulbs, annuals, irises, and perennial plantings designed by Gardens staff and students.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal display garden planted with bulbs, annuals, irises, and perennials.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers Gardens describes the Donald B. Lacey Display Garden as a seasonal garden maintained by staff and student horticulturists; Gardens admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday during Rutgers Gardens seasonal hours; flowering displays vary by season and plants may not be picked.

cards.title: Browse the Zimmerli Galleries
cards.subtitle: 71 Hamilton Street, College Avenue Campus
cards.notes: Meet in the lobby, choose a few galleries to explore at your own pace, and trade observations afterward rather than trying to see everything.
cards.short_summary: A public Rutgers art museum with free admission for all visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zimmerli Art Museum states that it is open to the public and offers free admission to all.
cards.access_notes: Open Wed.–Fri. 11 a.m.–6 p.m. and Sat.–Sun. noon–5 p.m.; closed Mondays, Tuesdays, and listed holidays. Check gallery closures before visiting.

cards.access_notes: Third floor, North Wing, on the George Street side. Open access; one Alexander study-room booking per NetID per day, maximum three hours.

cards.notes: Use the dry-erase board and request markers, a surge protector, or laptop speakers from the desk when preparing a small group project.

cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 301E is a four-seat group-study space on Alexander Library's third-floor North Wing; it has a dry-erase board and offers markers, a surge protector, and laptop speakers for checkout.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Rutgers–New Brunswick songs, ceremonies, legends, and recurring campus traditions.

cards.entity_name: On the Banks of the Old Raritan
cards.title: Sing “On the Banks”
cards.subtitle: Rutgers alma mater
cards.notes: Learn the current alma mater words before a campus ceremony or game, then listen for the familiar refrain about the old Raritan.
cards.short_summary: Rutgers’ alma mater began as a Glee Club commission in 1873 and remains a school-song tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers says its school-song tradition dates to 1873 and identifies “On the Banks of the Old Raritan” as the alma mater.
cards.source_title: Rutgers Traditional Songs, Lyrics, Alma Mater
cards.access_notes: Listen or sing along at public university events where it is performed; participation is optional.

cards.title: Answer “RU Rah, Rah!”
cards.subtitle: Rutgers fight song
cards.notes: At a Rutgers football game, listen for the “RU Rah, Rah!” chant drawn from the fight song and join only if you want to.
cards.short_summary: The fight song connects a football-game chant to the Old Queens bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers states that students chant “RU Rah, Rah!” at football games from the fight song “The Bells Must Ring.”
cards.source_title: Rutgers Traditional Songs, Lyrics, Alma Mater
cards.access_notes: Game admission policies vary; the chant itself requires no purchase.

cards.title: Try the Rutgers History Lesson
cards.subtitle: Traditional Rutgers song
cards.notes: Read the lyrics as a compact tour of Rutgers’ Dutch heritage, Revolutionary-era history, and the 1869 Princeton game.
cards.short_summary: A school song turns Rutgers history into a call-and-response-style campus artifact.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers describes “The Rutgers History Lesson” as one of its traditional songs and says it explores Dutch heritage and Revolutionary War participation.
cards.source_title: Rutgers Traditional Songs, Lyrics, Alma Mater
cards.access_notes: Lyrics are publicly available through Rutgers; no event attendance is required to explore it.

cards.title: Ring in and ring out
cards.subtitle: New Student Convocation and Commencement
cards.notes: If you are participating in Convocation or Commencement, look for the Red Lion Bell and follow event staff guidance for ringing it.
cards.short_summary: Students mark the start and completion of their Rutgers studies by ringing a replica bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers says incoming students ring the Red Lion Bell at New Student Convocation and graduating students may ring it at New Brunswick Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Available in connection with the relevant university ceremonies; follow ceremony access rules.

cards.title: Mind the Queens Campus gates
cards.subtitle: Hamilton Street, Queens Campus
cards.notes: Walk the historic Queens Campus route, but note the student superstition about passing beneath the Class of 1902 Memorial Gateway before graduation.
cards.short_summary: A graduation-timing superstition is attached to one of Rutgers’ historic campus gateways.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers notes a superstition that students who walk beneath the gate before commencement will not graduate on time.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use public walkways and respect campus access guidance.

cards.title: Circle Passion Puddle—if you believe
cards.subtitle: Cook/Douglass campus, off Red Oak Lane
cards.notes: Visit the pond for its long-standing Cook–Douglass legend: walking around it three times while holding hands was said to predict marriage.
cards.short_summary: A campus pond anchors a distinctly Rutgers courtship legend.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers documents the long-standing legend that a Cook student and Douglass student walking hand-in-hand around the pond three times would marry.
cards.source_title: Rutgers’ Passion Puddle Among America’s Most Romantic College Spots
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; the legend is folklore, not a promise or requirement.

cards.title: See Ag Field Day within Rutgers Day
cards.subtitle: George H. Cook Campus
cards.notes: Plan for the spring Rutgers Day program and look for the Cook Campus animal fitting and exhibition contests during Ag Field Day.
cards.short_summary: A century-old agricultural outreach day persists as part of the universitywide Rutgers Day celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers identifies the 2026 event as the 107th Annual Rutgers Day/Ag Field Day and describes student animal exhibition contests on Cook Campus.
cards.access_notes: Annual spring event; confirm the next program and access details before going.

cards.title: Serve on Scarlet Day
cards.subtitle: Rutgers–New Brunswick and New Jersey community sites
cards.notes: Watch for fall or spring registration, then choose a service assignment supporting cleanup, outdoor revitalization, youth, or older adults.
cards.short_summary: RUPA’s recurring service day sends Rutgers–New Brunswick volunteers into New Jersey communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers says Scarlet Day of Service is a campus-wide, day-long Rutgers–New Brunswick event hosted by RUPA in both fall and spring semesters.
cards.access_notes: Registration and project locations are announced each semester; choose an assignment with appropriate transportation and accessibility.

cards.title: Mark graduation with a Kente Stole
cards.subtitle: Pre-commencement ceremony for Rutgers–New Brunswick graduates
cards.notes: Eligible graduates can register for this pre-commencement celebration, whose culminating tradition includes a Kente Stole presentation.
cards.short_summary: An annual ceremony celebrates graduating students and African diaspora and Latine cultural traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers describes its annual Rites of Passage as a pre-commencement celebration that culminates with a Kente Stole presentation.
cards.access_notes: For eligible New Brunswick degree recipients; the cited 2026 event was open to all graduating students.

cards.title: Close out with Senior Days
cards.subtitle: Rutgers–New Brunswick graduating class events
cards.notes: Graduating seniors can check the annual schedule for class events, including the cap-decorating gathering and other final-days activities.
cards.short_summary: Student Affairs organizes a multi-event sendoff for each Rutgers graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: Rutgers–New Brunswick Student Affairs describes Senior Days as a series of events for each graduating class and lists a 2026 cap-decorating event.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors; individual events can have separate registration or ticket requirements.
